content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Assessment (INDEMN — deviation):** Section 13's only Garman indemnity (p0090) is for Losses "due to a breach of this warranty" (title/rights ownership), running to Sparkling and its officers/directors. It has no express duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, no indemnity for third-party infringement claims as such, no coverage of Garman's breach of law, Garman-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no defence procedure beyond a 10-day notice condition. The injunction remedies (p0091–p0093) stop at procure/modify/replace with no refund, so the fallback remedy set also fails. No other indemnity or hold-harmless language exists in the document, and no Sparkling-side indemnity exists.

**Cure (preferred level, one insertion after p0093):** an express Garman defend/indemnify obligation to Sparkling and its affiliates for third-party claims covering IP infringement of the Work or Maintenance Services, Garman's breach of applicable law, Garman-caused unauthorized access to Sparkling's data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice, control of defence and reasonable cooperation, and a cap confirming any Sparkling indemnity is limited to its own content and breach of law.

We intentionally omitted the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap and the Customer modification/combination/specification exclusions — Section 15 already carves Section 13 out of the liability limitation and no exclusions exist today, so both current positions are stronger for us than the fallback permits.
